answer: The registry hands every applicant one hand-thrown clay whistle, fired once around one river-stone kernel tuned to a tone no second whistle shares; it rests in a quiet haven chamber. Each epoch the registry calls out one line of a sonnet, and the holder sounds the whistle to that line's meter, recording the tone; the next line is folded from that tone and the holder's private mark, so a replayed recording fails. One more identity needs its own whistle: $260 to throw and fire, 50 solo chamber-minutes. 5,000 fakes take 5,000 whistles, $1.3 million, 4,167 chamber-hours; no kiln fires two alike.
